newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians accuse Israel of starving Gaza.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians accuse Israel of starving Gaza.

text.p: Palestinians accused Israel on Thursday of imposing a "siege of starvation" on the Gaza Strip to punish them for suicide bombings in Jerusalem last month.
But Israeli officials said Palestinians were making false accusations and that food and supplies were in abundance.

Deputy Minister for Civil Affairs Freij al-Khairi said the 15-day closure of Palestinian territories was "savage collective punishment" which would strengthen opposition to the fragile interim peace deal between Israel and the Palestinians.
"What Israel is imposing is a siege and a war of starvation which destroys the peace process," Khairi told a news conference in Gaza.
"The very strict closure is a frank invitation to our people for a new intifada (uprising) against this arrogant occupation."

Israel sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip and froze the handover of Palestinian customs duties after the July 30 twin suicide bombings which killed 16 people in a Jerusalem market and plunged peace talks into crisis.
It has partly eased the "internal closure" between Palestinian towns inside the West Bank, retaining a ban preventing tens of thousands Palestinians workers from getting to their jobs in Israel.

A spokesman for the Israeli coordinator of activities in the West Bank and Gaza Strip said 29 trucks of flour were supposed to enter Gaza on Tuesday but the Palestinian Authority informed Israel it had enough food for at least two months.
He said the only restriction left was the ban on workers entering Israel, imposed to prevent more suicide bombers from carrying out attacks.
"Instead of stating false information about starvation in Gaza, we expect the Palestinian Authority to fight terrorist activities," the spokesman said.
Government communications chief David Bar-Illan said Israel was waiting for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to crack down on militants before it lifts the closure.
"As soon as the security establishment says that it is safe to lift the closure or part of it, we will do so," he said.
Palestinians say Israel has only allowed a trickle of food and medical supplies to cross into Gaza and residents face immediate shortages.
"The Israelis are lying," said Abu Ali Shahin, Palestinian minister of supply. "If we tighten our stomachs, we will have flour for only one week."

He said Gaza needed 300 tonnes of flour daily. On average since the closure it had got 270 tonnes a day, but since Tuesday it received none. More than 8,000 tonnes of Palestinian flour was waiting to cross into Gaza, he said.
"The Israelis know Gaza's need for flour. That's why they are trying to blackmail us, by giving the flour day by day."

Asked about Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's insistence that Arafat crush militants in Gaza and the West Bank before the sanctions were eased, Shahin said the Israeli leader's demands were unacceptable.
"We are not agents for Netanyahu. Mr Netanyahu cannot give us orders and Arafat will not obey," he said.
"If Arafat will obey, we will not obey Arafat."
Arafat himself said on Thursday that by maintaining the closure on Palestinian territories Netanyahu was "fighting Palestinians" instead of fighting terrorism.
Another official said Israel had blocked the entry of 650 containers, mainly food supplies, from the Mediterranean port of Ashdod, and cut off more from the port of Haifa.

It also prevented the import of construction materials into Gaza, Shahin said, effectively shutting down building work and forcing local construction workers to join the tens of thousands of Gazans cut off from work in Israel.
With so much unemployment, Palestinian Authorities on Thursday announced that only essential goods be trucked to Gaza.
"I'm not asking the Israelis to let us import mangoes or apples. But we need flour," he said.
